sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

2. Petitioners claim title over the land in question which has been acquired under the Railways Act,
1989.
3.

It is the case of the petitioners that without giving an opportunity of hearing to the petitioners to object such acquisition and preparation of the award in favour of respondent Nos.5, 6 and 7, the award has been prepared.

The petitioners immediately, after preparation of the award objected, but the District Land Acquisition Officer, Giridih has referred the matter to the Civil Court, only in respect of the structure which stands over the land in question, though the petitioners is claiming title over the entire land and property.

4. Learned counsel for the respondents-State submits that there is serious dispute with regard to the title between the petitioners and the awardee, which cannot be decided by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Giridih, thus, the matter has been referred to the Civil Court.
5. After going through the records, I find that there is serious dispute in respect of title.
The petitioners are claiming title over the land and property in question based on the registered sale deed of 1951.
The awardee is also claiming themselves as dar-raiyat, thus claiming compensation.

sentences.text: Since there is a dispute in respect of title of the property including the construction, the matter has already been referred to the learned Principal District & Sessions Judge, Giridih.
I find no illegality in the said process.

It is expected that the said reference would be registered and after hearing, an appropriate decision would be taken by the learned Principal District & Sessions Judge,
Giridih.

7. It would be open to the learned Principal District & Sessions Judge, Giridih to pass any interim order, even restraining withdrawal of the aforesaid amount by any of the parties, till final decision of the reference.
8. With aforesaid observations, the instant writ petition is disposed of.

(ANANDA SEN, J.) R.S.
